sentences.text: This animal is considered one of the oldest known stegosaurs, alongside Thyreosaurus, and stands as the oldest definitive stegosaur found anywhere in the world.
It holds the distinction of being the first described eurypodan dinosaur taxon discovered in North Africa.
Susannah Maidment, Thomas J. Raven, Driss Ouarhache, and Paul M. Barrett described Adratiklit boulahfa on August 16, 2019, based on a single dorsal vertebra cataloged as NHMUK PV R37366.
The Natural History Museum in the United Kingdom acquired this specific specimen from fossil traders.
Other known specimens represent multiple individuals, estimated to be around five, including a fossilized humerus measuring 61 centimeters in length.
The unique skeletal traits identified in Adratiklit are diagnostic for the entire Stegosauria group.

Adratiklit is classified within the subfamily Dacentrurinae, being more closely related to European stegosaurs like Dacentrurus and Miragaia than to southern African taxa, and belongs to the family Stegosauridae.

Adratiklit lived on the supercontinent Gondwana during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age, in what is now Africa. Remains were found in the El Mers Group, likely the El Mers II Formation, near Boulahfa, south of Boulemane in Fès-Meknes, Morocco. The animal lived during the middle Jurassic period, approximately between 168 and 166 million years ago, and lived from the Bathonian to the Callovian stages, between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago.
